Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:10:1.english: [As for] writing, how do we write - A verdict in a case where there is a dispute and they inclined after the majority.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:11:2.hebrew: מדבריהם נזדכה - משמע שהיה מחלוקת ביניהם, ומתוך דבריהם נזדכה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:11:2.english: From their words he was deemed exempt - This implies that there was a dispute among them, and out of their words he was deemed exempt.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:12:1.hebrew: לשלומי איהו מנתא בהדייהו - אם טעו השנים וחייבין לשלם מביתם, פליגי הנך רבנן בדיין השלישי, אם ישלם חלקו עמהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:12:1.english: For him to pay a portion along with them - If the two [judges] erred and are liable to pay from their [own] property, these Sages disagree regarding the third judge, whether he must pay his portion along with them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:12:2.hebrew: מאן דאמר זכאי - כתבינן, ולא כתבינן פלוגתייהו; דקסבר: כולם שוין, ואף השלישי ישלם עמהם, דאי לא הוה איהו בהדייהו — בתרי לא הוה מיפסיק דינא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:12:2.english: The one who says "Exempt" - [Meaning that] we write [this], and we do not write their dispute; for he maintains that they are all equal, and even the third [judge] must pay with them, for had he not been with them, the verdict could not have been decided with two [judges].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:14:1.english: For them to pay - To the litigant, the portion of the third judge.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:14:2.hebrew: למאן דאמר פלוני ופלוני מזכין כו' לא משלמי - דלהכי כתבינן פלוגתא בהדיא, לאודועי דבתרי נגמר דינא, ולא קיבלו עלייהו כולי דינא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:14:2.english: According to the one who says: “So-and-so and so-and-so deem [him] exempt, etc.,” they do not pay - For this is why we write the dispute explicitly: to make known that the judgment was concluded by two [judges], and they did not accept upon themselves the entire judgment.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:19:1.hebrew: התם קיימי - דהא לא קתני מתני' שיוציאום לאחר ששמעו דבריהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:19:1.english: They were standing there - For the Mishnah did not teach that they should remove them after they heard their words.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:1:1.hebrew: וכל לישני דבי דינא - כל דבריהם היו כתובין בלשון ב"ד, ולא היו חתומין אלא שנים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:1:1.english: And all the formulations of the court - All their words were written in the language of a court, and only two were signed [on it].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:1:2.hebrew: ולא הוה כתיב ביה במותב תלתא הוינא וחד ליתוהי - כדמצרכינן בכתובות (דף כב.) בשלשה שישבו לקיים את השטר, ומת אחד מהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:1:2.english: And it was not written in it: “We were in a session of three, and one is no [longer here]” - As we require in Ketubot (22a) regarding three [judges] who sat to validate a document, and one of them died.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:20:1.hebrew: לימא דלא כר' נתן - דהא מתני' קתני דלעיילינהו לסהדי, משום דמתחילה כשבדקום, שמעו דבריו של זה בלא זה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:20:1.english: Shall we say [that it is] not in accordance with Rabbi Natan - For the Mishnah teaches that they bring in the witnesses, because initially, when they examined them, they heard the words of this [witness] without that [one].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:20:2.hebrew: עד שיראו שניהם כאחת - את העדות, ולקמן יליף טעמא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:20:2.english: Unless the two of them see together - the [matter of] testimony; and later on, [the Gemara] derives the reason.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:21:1.hebrew: אין עדותן מתקיימת בב"ד - לפסוק הדין על פיהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:21:1.english: Their testimony does not stand in court - To render judgment based on their [testimony].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:21:2.hebrew: עד שיעידו שניהם כאחת - וסתמא היא, ולא ר' יהושע בן קרחה קאמר לה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:21:2.english: Unless the two of them testify as one - And it is an anonymous [statement], and it is not Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa who said it.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:22:1.english: And it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Neḥemya - For he said [that] at the time of deliberation, they would remove the litigants.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:24:1.hebrew: במאי קמיפלגי - ת"ק ור' יהושע:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:24:1.english: With regard to what do they disagree - The first tanna and Rabbi Yehoshua.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:25:1.hebrew: אמנה דקא מסהיד האי כו' - זה אומר: בפני הלוהו מנה, וזה אומר: בפני הלוהו מנה; זה לא ראה של זה — נמצא שאין כאן עדות שלם במנה אחד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:25:1.english: About the one hundred dinars that this one is testifying, etc. - This [witness] says: "In my presence he lent him a maneh," and that [witness] says: "In my presence he lent him a maneh"; this [one] did not see [the loan witnessed by] that [one] — it turns out that there is no complete testimony here regarding a single maneh.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:25:2.hebrew: ואידך - מ"מ, תרווייהו מסהדי דמנה קא רשי ביה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:25:2.english: And the other - In any event, both of them testify that [the creditor] has a claim of a maneh against him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:26:1.hebrew: והוא עד - והאי קרא בשני עדים משתעי לגבי קרבן שבועת העדות, דאילו השביע עד אחד ולא העידו — פטור:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:26:1.english: And he is a witness - And this verse speaks of two witnesses with regard to the sacrifice for an oath of testimony, for if he adjured a single witness and he did not testify for him, [the witness] is exempt.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:27:1.english: As it is taught: “By inference, from that which is stated,” etc. - [The word] “witness” implies a single witness.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:29:1.english: And the Merciful One expresses it in the singular form - As it is written: “And he is a witness” (Leviticus 5:1).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:2:1.hebrew: היינו דריש לקיש - דאמר: חזקה אין ב"ד כותבין שטר אלא כדת וכהלכה, והני וודאי תלתא הוו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:2:1.english: This is [the statement] of Reish Lakish - Who said: [There is a] presumption that a court does not write a document unless [it is] in accordance with the law and proper practice, and these [judges] were certainly three.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:2:2.english: For an erroneous court - [Who] think that two [judges] are qualified to judge.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:31:1.hebrew: לשבועה אתי - עד אחד אינו מחייבו ממון, אלא שבועה. הלכך, כשהעיד זה יחידי וזה יחידי, לא שייכא תורת ממון בעדותן, ולא מצרפינן להו, דהא לאו לחיוביה ממונא אתו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:31:1.english: He comes to [impose] an oath - A single witness does not obligate him [to pay] money, but rather [to take] an oath. Therefore, when this [witness] testified individually and that [witness testified] individually, the category of monetary [matters] does not apply to their testimony, and we do not join them, for they did not come to obligate him [to pay] money.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:3:1.hebrew: בי דינא - הכל יודעין שאין שנים קרוים ב"ד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:3:1.english: A court - Everyone knows that two [judges] are not called a court.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:4:1.hebrew: בי דינא דרבנא אשי - דאינהו ודאי ידעי, שאין ב"ד קרויין בשנים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:4:1.english: The court of Rabbana Ashi - For they certainly knew that [a panel of] two is not called a court.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:5:1.hebrew: ואמר לן רבנא אשי - לכתוב כך. דכיון דהוא היה שם, מסתמא לא צוה לפחות משלשה לכתוב. והאי דנקט רב אשי — לפי שבית דינו היה ראש בימי רבינא, ושניהם סידרו גמרא של תלמוד בבלי, כדאמרינן התם (בהשוכר את הפועלים דף פו.): רב אשי ורבינא סוף הוראה; ובימיו נאמרו דברים הללו, והוקבעו בגמרא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:5:1.english: And Rabbana Ashi said to us - [He told us] to write thus. For since he was there, he presumably would not have instructed fewer than three to write. And that which [the Gemara] mentioned Rav Ashi is because his court was preeminent in the days of Ravina, and both of them arranged the Gemara of the Babylonian Talmud, as we say there (in HaSokher Et HaPo'alim, daf 86a): "Rav Ashi and Ravina are the end of instruction"; and in his days these matters were stated and established in the Gemara.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:6:1.hebrew: בבית לא אמר כלום - אינו נאמן, לפי שאין בידו ליטלן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:6:1.english: [If it was] in the house, he has said nothing - He is not believed, because it is not within his power to take them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:6:2.hebrew: בשדה דבריו קיימין - דמה לו לשקר? אם רוצה, נוטלן ונותנן לאותו שהוא מעיד עליו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:6:2.english: In the field, his statement stands - For why would he lie? If he wishes, he [could] take them and give them to that [person] on whose behalf he is testifying.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:8:1.english: If as one who relays - If he appeared to them as one who relays his words to his children in truth, in the language of a testament.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:8:2.hebrew: כמערים - שהוא מתיירא שלא יטלם בחייו, או שלא יחזיקוהו כעשיר להוסיף על יציאותיו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:8:2.english: As one who employs artifice - That he is afraid lest [someone] take them in his lifetime, or lest they consider him wealthy, [thereby] increasing his expenses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:9:1.english: That his father left him - And he did not tell them where they were.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:9:2.english: The master of the dream - The angel who shows dreams at night.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:9:3.english: Such and such they are - He tells him how much [money] there is.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 30a:9:4.english: Do not elevate, etc. - And he may spend them in their place [without having to bring them to Jerusalem].

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 30a:17:1.english: "Because it has the appearance of falsehood" - And [the prohibition] on account of "You shall not go as a talebearer" does not apply here.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 30a:5:1.hebrew: ודילמא רבנן דבי רב אשי כשמואל ס"ל - כשמואל קי"ל, כדפיר' בריש מכילתין (דף ג:). וה"פ: כשמואל בעלמא ס"ל באודיתא — שכתבו בהודאה בשנים בלא קנין; ובזה אין הלכה כמותו, כדאמר לעיל: "הודה בפני שנים, קנו מידו כותבין, ואם לאו אין כותבין":
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 30a:5:1.english: "And perhaps the Sages of the court of Rav Ashi hold like Shmuel" - [Yet] we rule in accordance with Shmuel, as we explained at the beginning of our tractate (3b)! And this is its explanation: [Perhaps] they held like Shmuel in general, [and applied his ruling] to an admission [odita] — that they wrote [a deed] for an admission before two without an act of acquisition [kinyan]; and in this [matter], the halakha is not like him, as [the Gemara] said above: "If one made an admission before two: [if] they performed an act of acquisition with him, they write; and if not, they do not write."

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 30a:7:1.hebrew: כל שאין בידו - ליכא למימר דלהמניה במיגו דאי בעי שתיק, דאין זה מיגו; דאי שתיק — מנחי התם, ולא יבא ליד פלוני:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 30a:7:1.english: "In any case where it is not in his power" - One cannot say that he should be believed through a miggo that had he wanted, he could have remained silent, for this is not a [valid] miggo; since had he remained silent, [the money] would remain lying there and would not come into the hands of so-and-so.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 30a:8:1.english: “And if as one who relays [information], his statement stands” - [The rationale of] “so as not to make his children appear sated” [i.e., wealthy] is not applicable here.
